images.filename: James K. Polk Building, Deaderick Street and 5th Avenue, Nashville, TN (54385244349).jpg
images.caption: Built in 1981, this Modern International and Brutalist building was designed by Taylor and Crabtree to serve as a government office building for the State of Tennessee, as well as the Tennessee Performing Arts Center, and was named for former US President James K. Polk.  The building stands 24 stories and 392 feet (119 meters) tall, and features a concrete-clad base made up of multiple geometric volumes with a corner lobby featuring a glass facade, contrasting with the concrete exterior of the rest of the lower portion of the building, a tower clad in glass that cantilevers out from a central concrete core, and an exposed steel truss structure at the roof of the tower, which supports the floors below.  The building today houses a live performing arts venue, as well as offices for the government of the state of Tennessee.

images.caption: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge - Nashville's most historically important honky-tonk was a favored watering hole for Tom T. Hall, Kris Kristofferson, Willie Nelson, Roger Miller and other legends who spilled from the Ryman's back door to greet the wee hours at Tootsie's. These days, the room is filled mostly by tourists, college kids and cowboys. It's still a blast to look around, though, even if that glut of tourists and college kids makes moving around nearly impossible night to night. The south side and roof of the Ryman Auditorum are visible behind Tootsie's.
